words.gloss: to those who do not have

literal: To those who do not have desire, suffering will not exist; if that exists, it will come without ceasing, more and more.
translation: For those who are free from desire, there is no suffering; but if desire exists, suffering will come upon them endlessly, more and more.
modern: ஆசை இல்லாதவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை; அந்த ஆசை இருக்குமானால், துன்பம் குறையாமல் மேலும் மேலும் வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the direct relationship between desire and suffering. For those who have completely eliminated desire (அவா), there is no sorrow in life. However, if desire is allowed to exist (அஃதுண்டேல்), suffering will continuously and endlessly (தவாஅது) multiply and come upon them (மேன்மேல் வரும்). The word 'தவாஅது' is a poetic form (alapeṭai) of 'தவாது', meaning 'without decreasing' or 'ceaselessly', emphasizing the relentless nature of desire-induced pain.
